title: QB9_H#q10 shipped candidate-visible editorial placeholders in place of the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 references
candidate_claim: The live card carried two editorial placeholders in candidate-facing text: '[cite the 2025 Act at Part level; the 1958 sections must not be quoted as current]' in the 60-second answer, and '[2025 Act - Part-level, sections pending verification]' or its equivalent in the 15-second answer, the Governing-instrument line, the Key Numbers list and the reg-box. A candidate-facing production answer must not ship with an editorial placeholder.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD. Five placeholder instances inside the q10 card block, all removed. Resolved by OUTCOME A of the two lawful outcomes - authoritative current evidence establishes the exact sections - not by outcome B.

authority.instrument: The Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 (Act No. 24 of 2025), India
authority.how_read: Part V (Seafarers), sections 54 onwards, read directly from the held Gazette PDF at 06-india-law-and-dg-shipping/Merchant-Shipping-Act-2025/_base/MS_Act_2025_A2025-24.pdf (sha256 6fb38616ed8b82ae7e831e5589ffd59a7b27e13d55b1728940fe25892f758f63), which DGMA publishes as the competent authority's own copy.
authority.blocker_that_was_cleared: SRC-MSACT-2025 recorded claims_NOT_established: 'Section numbers outside s.4 and s.5', with the revalidation note 'A corrigenda dated 30 September 2025 is listed on the same DGMA page and is NOT held. Obtain it before quoting any section verbatim beyond s.4.' That corrigenda has now been RETRIEVED from DGMA (sha256 4a28b152426b0cd709be37a4bc0c176be059f56eed97566fe96ed0b1bedcf818, 273992 bytes) and read in full. It makes exactly three purely typographical corrections - page 33 line 19 'matter' to 'matters'; page 69 line 24 'himself such' to 'himself of such'; page 71 line 12 'sea borne' to 'seaborne'. There is NO renumbering and no change to any section relied on here, so the hold that produced the placeholders is discharged on evidence rather than waived.

sections_now_cited.s.63(1): The master or owner of every Indian vessel, or the recruitment and placement service agency for an Indian or foreign vessel, shall enter into a seafarers' employment agreement in the prescribed form and manner with every seafarer engaged, and shall submit a copy to the shipping master.
sections_now_cited.s.63(2): Saving for a vessel registered at a port outside India whose agreement was made in due form according to the law of that port, for CDC-holding seafarers.
sections_now_cited.s.63(3): A seafarer shall, before signing, be given an opportunity to examine and seek advice on the agreement, to ensure he has freely entered into it with sufficient understanding of his rights and responsibilities.
sections_now_cited.s.64(1): Full payments due to seafarers at intervals not later than monthly, with a monthly account of payments due and amounts paid, including wages and additional payments.
sections_now_cited.s.83(1): A dispute arising under the agreement between master, ship owner or agent and a seafarer shall be submitted to the shipping master.
sections_now_cited.s.94(1): A seafarer is deemed a serving seafarer from the date of the agreement until thirty days after final discharge from it.

authority.deliberately_not_cited: No section outside Part V is asserted, and s.78(1)(e) (the MLC Part A rule-making hook) is not put in front of the candidate because the card is about where entitlement lives, not about delegated legislation. Nothing was reconstructed from the 1958 Act.

propagation.no_supersession_needed: QB9_H#q10 is pinned by NO manifest. It is named in the prose notes of batch_h3a_manifest.json and batch_h6_manifest.json as the card that already answers AUG-0140, but neither record carries a digest for it, so no chain is created and none is required.
propagation.scope_pass: The full candidate-facing placeholder sweep across all 234 meoclass1/ and SQ/ HTML files is reported separately - see the note field. Only the q10 instances are corrected here.

invariants: The card's core answer is unchanged: the SEA is the seafarer's individual employment instrument; an applicable CBA may be incorporated or referenced; the onboard copy and PSC access under MLC Std A2.1; wage accounts under Std A2.2; the neutral discharge record under A2.1.3; and the individual SEA distinguished from the DMLC and company procedure.
The classical articles-of-agreement layer, the Shipping Master's role and the CE Oral Tip (Paul) are unchanged.
This was NOT expanded into a new MLC card, and no new card was created.
The standing warning not to carry 1958 numbering across is preserved in the 60-second answer and the Key Numbers list.
content_index_effect: None on counts. QB9_H#q10 keeps its id, anchor, question text and topic.
note: SCOPE BOUNDARY, STATED. The sweep found the same 'pending verification' construction in 22 further candidate-facing places - QB9_H's other cards (notably #q4, #q8, #q11 and the reg-boxes around them), QB1_I (3), QB3_J (1), QB5_B_CheatSheet (1), QB9_D (1) and QB9_H_CheatSheet (1). Those are NOT corrected here, because the authorisation is three items and because they are a different thing from a placeholder in kind: an imperative instruction to the author ('[cite the 2025 Act...]') is scaffolding, whereas '(exact 2025 section pending verification)' is an honest candidate-facing currentness caveat. They are nevertheless bracketed editorial text on paid cards and are reported for Founder sizing. QB9_H_CheatSheet's line telling the candidate to cite the Act at Part level with sections pending verification is left standing DELIBERATELY: it describes the whole QB9_H page, and only q10 has been resolved, so editing it would claim a resolution the page has not got.
